pull.title: common: drop locale setting hack
pull.body:
This was added to work around `boost::filesystem` throwing when the environments locale was invalid. Boost.Filesystem has been removed, and `std::filesystem` doesn't use the locale on POSIX (and bitcoind never calls `setlocale`).

Qt calls `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` on startup, and falls back to `C.UTF-8` if the locale isn't `UTF-8`.

Alternative to #36399, which extends the hack further.

events.body:
> Qt calls `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` on startup, and falls back to `C.UTF-8` if the locale isn't `UTF-8`.

Can you add a reference/source to this claim?

> Can you add a reference/source to this claim?

https://github.com/qt/qtbase/blob/37a9bf670e422daa20c1806fc873c27b35fb287d/src/corelib/kernel/qcoreapplication.cpp#L571-L639

We also claim this in: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/60ebd98c79043e99c582bcbaf412bc424c8daf9b/src/qt/bitcoin.cpp#L203
Doesn’t this change affect the behaviour of the scripts specified via the `-*notify` options in environments where the locale is invalid?

Yes, that is also what Ralph says (https://git.fish.foo/bitcoin/bitcoin/pulls/36524#author-ralph) , but I think users are better off not setting an invalid locale. If they really want to set an invalid locale, they are better off setting the locale in their notify script explicitly. (Explicitly setting it works before and after the changes here)

Concept ACK

This surfaces an already buggy test, that now fails on some local environments, see comment.

comments.body:
This surfaces a bug in `interface_gui.py`, that passes on `master` but fails on 622df9e941dd55fc9b01125ea1de659ed6a9794e.

On CI, we set `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` in all scripts, so the locale is set in all tests, which means that we're not really testing this change.

When running this test locally on a Linux environment with `LC_ALL` unset and no `nl_NL.UTF-8` locale installed, the `interface_gui.py` test fails. This is because in `test_node.py:302`, we set `subp_env.setdefault("LC_ALL", "nl_NL.UTF-8")`. On CI, this operation is a no-op because `LC_ALL` is always set, so the `nl_NL.UTF-8` locale is never actually set. When it is actually set, and `nl_NL.UTF-8` isn't installed on the machine, the test fails.

Tested in a `debian:trixie` container:

The test runs fine with `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 python3 build/test/functional/interface_gui.py`.

From #35551, it seems like we set a well-translated language to ensure that in a foreign locale, RPC strings still come through in English. If that's what we want to achieve, then perhaps we could e.g. add https://github.com/stickies-v/bitcoin/commit/a39fa5420ed965f8975221ce49bd813fac3aed61 as a minimal fix prior to this change?
